items.title: RBI turns to 30-day VRRR to absorb excess liquidity
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India is conducting auctions to absorb excess funds. This liquidity stems from special dollar mobilization programs and forex inflows. The central bank aims to manage surplus funds and control inflation pressures. Analysts expect liquidity to potentially reach fifteen lakh crore rupees soon. RBI also sold government papers to manage market liquidity effectively.

items.title: NCLAT sets aside Zaveri Group's bid for Gujarat Hydrocarbons and Power SEZ
items.summary: The NCLAT has overturned Zaveri Group's resolution plan for GHPSL. This decision mandates a restart of the insolvency process with new bids. The appellate tribunal cited an unverified presumption regarding SEZ de-notification. It also highlighted errors in the initial information memorandum provided. Consequently, fresh expressions of interest will now be invited.

items.title: World's biggest wealth fund plans to cut government bonds, US Treasuries face $75 billion impact
items.summary: Norway's $2.3 trillion sovereign wealth fund plans to cut government bonds from 70% to 50% of its portfolio to diversify risk and boost returns. This change could significantly impact US Treasuries, with holdings projected to drop by $75 billion, pending government approval.

items.title: Gland Pharma block deal: Fosun Pharma divests 99 lakh shares worth Rs 2,800 crore
items.summary: Fosun Pharma sold a 6% stake in Gland Pharma for ₹2,800 crore via a block deal, reducing its holding to 45.77%. Major buyers included Kotak, Axis, and ICICI Prudential Mutual Funds, while Gland Pharma shares closed higher at ₹2,932.40.

items.title: Maharashtra pitches for Belgium investments
items.summary: Maharashtra's Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis invited Belgian companies to explore investment opportunities within the state, positioning the state as an essential hub for engaging with global markets. With the India-EU free trade agreement poised to enhance trade relations significantly, Belgium's Prime Minister Bart De Wever echoed the sentiment.

items.title: Lululemon’s turnaround gets tougher as new CEO inherits a battered brand
items.summary: Lululemon shares dropped significantly after the company lowered its full-year sales forecast. The sportswear maker's signature leggings business saw a notable sales decline. Competitors like Alo and Vuori are gaining market share in athleisure. New CEO Heidi O'Neill faces challenges in regaining customer relevance and sales growth. The company has financial flexibility for a potential operational realignment and cost adjustments.

items.title: Pulse of the Street: US bond yields, interest rate jitters drag Indian equities lower this week
items.summary: Indian equities fell about 1% this week as higher US Treasury yields, elevated crude prices and foreign selling weighed on sentiment. Friday’s recovery offered little relief, with valuations, IPO supply and shifting rate expectations keeping investors cautious for the week ahead.

items.title: NSE IPO listing date, timeline: When ₹30,000 cr issue is expected to hit Indian stock market exchanges
items.summary: The NSE IPO, approved by Sebi, is set to raise around ₹30,000 crore, surpassing previous IPO records. Offering 149 million shares from existing shareholders, the IPO marks a significant milestone after years of delays due to regulatory issues and is expected to list in September 2024.

items.title: BSNL's homegrown 4G network carries 6 PB data per day: C-DoT
items.summary: BSNL's indigenous 4G network is handling six petabytes of data daily. The network supports 1.75 lakh 4G base stations across one lakh sites. High-definition voice calls are now enabled through IP Multimedia Subsystem deployment. Indigenous 5G RAN technology is currently undergoing live testing on BSNL's network. BSNL aims to compete with private operators using its domestically developed mobile network.

items.title: SAIL output grows 8 per cent in August; sales up 13 per cent
items.summary: Steel Authority of India Limited has announced an impressive eight percent increase in crude steel production, with total sales surging by thirteen percent in the same timeframe. Notably, the company has made substantial reductions in its overall borrowings. This financial enhancement comes after the reporting date of March 31, 2026. SAIL continues to hold its status as a top player in India's steel industry.

The company will also recruit 40 additional full-time employees to support the expanded operations.

items.title: US stocks today: S&P 500, Dow stocks slip as stronger jobs report lifts rate-hike bets
items.summary: US stocks slipped after a stronger-than-expected August jobs report boosted bets on a Fed rate hike in September. The S&P 500 and Dow fell, while investors turned their focus to next week’s inflation data. Lululemon, Adobe and credit-reporting stocks also declined, adding to market pressure.

items.title: Air India terminates Phuket-Delhi flight pilot after testing positive for drugs
items.summary: Air India terminated a pilot's employment after a positive drug test. The pilot was in command of a Phuket to Delhi flight. This action follows Air India's strict zero-tolerance safety policy. The airline confirmed the pilot's employment termination with immediate effect. This incident highlights the airline's commitment to regulatory compliance.

items.title: Lupin gets USFDA approval for Modafinil tablets to treat excessive sleepiness
items.summary: Pharmaceutical major Lupin announced its USFDA approval for Modafinil tablets. These tablets are used to treat excessive sleepiness in adult patients. The approved drug is bioequivalent to Provigil Tablets of Nuvo Pharmaceuticals. Modafinil tablets had estimated annual sales of USD 70.7 million in the United States. Lupin currently operates 15 manufacturing facilities globally.

items.title: Belgian PM De Wever pitches lower, zero tariffs to boost India-EU trade
items.summary: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever urged further cuts in import duties between India and the EU. He specifically highlighted the diamond sector for potential zero tariffs after a new trade agreement. This landmark pact, signed this year, aims to boost bilateral trade significantly. Indian diamantaires have established strong ties with Antwerp, Belgium's diamond hub. The partnership between India and Belgium in gems and jewellery is substantial and growing.

The company is setting up manufacturing and integration operations in Pune, Maharashtra, with ambitions to create a comprehensive energy storage platform in India, catering to the growing demand for renewable energy and enhancing grid reliability.

items.title: US diesel prices hit a record high, pushing up transportation costs for a long list of goods
items.summary: Diesel prices soared to unprecedented levels in the United States on Friday, primarily due to the six-month conflict involving Iran. This rise in costs is causing transportation fees for everyday goods and services to climb, with businesses now shifting these costs onto consumers via various surcharges. If diesel prices continue on this trajectory, consumers might face even more significant price hikes ahead.

This significant public issue follows years of regulatory delays and scrutiny.

items.title: Mamaearth parent Honasa Consumer targets Rs 5,500 cr revenue by FY31
items.summary: Honasa Consumer expects revenue to double to Rs 5,550 crore by FY31. The company also targets an Ebitda margin of 15 percent during the same period. Growth will focus on existing popular categories and expanding into new ones. Mamaearth, the flagship brand, is showing renewed growth in key segments. Honasa Consumer intends to capture the surging online retail wave in India.

items.summary: Indian equity markets ended Friday with a relief rally, led by metal and banking stocks, as concerns over an imminent US Fed rate hike eased. Nifty gained 0.1%, while Sensex rose 0.48%. SBI Life and Tata Steel were among the top gainers, while HCL Tech and Bharti Airtel declined.

items.title: India bonds slip for third week tracking oil, global debt rout
items.summary: Indian government bonds have witnessed a third straight week of decline, influenced by escalating oil prices and expectations of global interest rate hikes. Despite some domestic liquidity cushioning the Indian debt market, concerns over inflation and fiscal stability loom large due to rising crude prices. Investors are now keenly awaiting forthcoming inflation data and the outcomes of central bank policy meetings.

items.title: Insurer can't reject claim if alcohol habit disclosed before policy purchase: Consumer commission
items.summary: A consumer commission ordered Edelweiss Tokio Life Insurance to pay over fifty lakh rupees. The company rejected a widow's claim despite disclosed alcohol consumption by her husband. Hypertension and diabetes were also noted as lifestyle diseases by the commission. The insurer was found guilty of deficiency in service for rejecting the claim. The widow will receive the claim amount, interest, and compensation for harassment.

items.title: E-commerce exports to help increase business of small-town players, says experts
items.summary: Government e-commerce measures will significantly boost small-town traders' global market access. Artisans in handlooms, handicrafts, and jewellery can now reach overseas buyers more easily. Reliable cross-border payment infrastructure is crucial for growing export volumes and international sales. This shift could transform India's export value and economic activity locations. India aims for USD 350 billion in e-commerce goods exports by 2030.

items.title: India debt investors call for higher short-term borrowing to absorb excess cash: Report
items.summary: Market analysis indicates that there is a strong call for the government to boost the supply of short-duration bonds. Lenders, benefiting from excess rupee liquidity, are actively seeking viable investment options. In light of a pronounced increase in banking system liquidity surplus, the government is currently reviewing its fiscal second-half borrowing schedule, which is to be revealed later this month.

The massive foreign currency inflows and the following dollar-rupee swaps are contributing to the massive liquidity overhang.

items.title: CG Power and Industrial Solutions starts production at new Madhya Pradesh facility
items.summary: CG Power and Industrial Solutions announced the first power transformer rollout from its new Sehore facility. This facility is India's largest single-location power transformer manufacturing plant. It can produce thirty-five power transformers monthly, ranging from 220 kV to 1,200 kV. The new plant will create over two thousand direct and indirect jobs in Sehore. Madhya Pradesh's Chief Minister attended the event and spoke about development.

items.title: India's forex reserves rise by $11.47 billion to hit record high of $740.80 billion as of August 28
items.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves saw a substantial increase of $11.475 billion. This brought the total reserves to $740.8 billion by August 28. The Reserve Bank of India monitors foreign exchange market developments closely. It intervenes when necessary to ensure orderly market conditions. The central bank refrains from targeting any specific exchange rate.

items.title: Mega NSE IPO coming as Sebi approves Rs 30,000 crore public offer
items.summary: NSE’s long-awaited IPO has moved closer after Sebi approved its draft offer plan for a proposed Rs 30,000-crore issue. The IPO will be entirely an offer for sale, allowing existing shareholders to dilute their stakes. The listing would mark the end of a process first initiated in 2016 and stalled over regulatory concerns.

items.summary: PVP Ventures stock price jumped significantly, offering shareholders a 143% return in a month. The company, focused on urban infrastructure, is regaining momentum and reported a net profit turnaround, attracting retail investors, while a positive credit rating enhanced its trading activity.

The Indira Gandhi International Airport experienced significant waterlogging after the intense downpour. A red alert was issued by the India Meteorological Department for thunderstorms and gusty winds. Passengers were advised to check flight statuses and allow extra travel time. Flight schedules faced disruptions due to the adverse weather conditions across the capital.
